# Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl

> A typesafe DSL for building and reading Excel workbooks (.xlsx/.xlsm), interpreted into
> calls against the DocumentFormat.OpenXml SDK. Most Excel libraries only go one direction -
> build a workbook from scratch, or mutate an existing one, through an imperative API. This
> one also round-trips (read a file back into the same immutable model) and can decompile a
> loaded workbook back into equivalent, runnable F# or C# source via built-in code
> generation - available as library calls, as MCP tools for an agent, and as a
> `fsopenxmldsl-mcp convert` CLI command for anyone else. A third surface (`Xml.fs`) does
> the same translation to/from plain XML against a real, embedded schema, for a caller who'd
> rather generate/consume data than code at all. Ships as three packages from one repo: the
> F# core (`Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl`), an idiomatic C# wrapper over it
> (`Kookerella.CsOpenXmlDsl`), and a local MCP server exposing it as agent tools/a CLI
> (`Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl.Mcp`).

License: MIT. Repo: `github.com/Kookerella-Ltd/Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl`. If a caller/agent
is working in **F#**, use `Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl` directly (full feature set, see below).
If working in **C#**, prefer `Kookerella.CsOpenXmlDsl` — a genuinely idiomatic, immutable,
fluent wrapper (records, `with`-expression-based fluent methods), not just an assembly
reference to the F# core: referencing `Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl` directly from C# is
possible but considerably less pleasant (F# discriminated unions and `option` types don't
translate cleanly). The C# wrapper now covers every feature the F# core models — see its
own section below for details.

## F# core: `Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl`

Root namespace: `Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl` (internals under `.Interpreter`, not public API).
Target frameworks: `net8.0`, `net10.0`.

### Core model

- `Workbook = { Sheets: Worksheet list; DefinedNames: DefinedNameEntry list; Protection: WorkbookProtection option; VbaProject: byte[] option }`
- `Worksheet` holds a sparse `Cell list` plus per-feature fields (`Tables`, `Charts`,
  `Images`, `PivotTables`, `SparklineGroups`, `ConditionalFormats`, `DataValidations`,
  `Hyperlinks`, `Comments`, `PageSetup`, `Protection`, `MergedRanges`, `FreezePane`,
  `AutoFilter`, `ColumnProps`, `RowProps`).
- `CellValue = Empty | Text of string | Number of float | Boolean of bool | Date of DateTime | Formula of expression: string * cachedValue: float option`
- `CellRef` is a zero-based `{ Row: int; Col: int }`; convert via `CellRef.ofA1 "B3"` / `CellRef.toA1 ref`.

### Entry points (`Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl.Api`, module `Workbook`)

- `Workbook.save (path: string) (wb: Workbook) : unit`
- `Workbook.saveToStream (stream: Stream) (wb: Workbook) : unit`
- `Workbook.load (path: string) : Workbook`
- `Workbook.loadFromStream (stream: Stream) : Workbook`
- `Workbook.generateScript (referenceLines: string list) (outputFileName: string) (wb: Workbook) : string`
  — renders `wb` as a self-contained `.fsx` that rebuilds an equivalent file when run via `dotnet fsi`.

### Building a workbook (the common path)

```fsharp
open Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl
open type Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl.SheetDsl

let data =
    sheet "Sheet1"
        [ row [ cell (Text "Name"); cell (Text "Amount") ]
          row [ cell (Text "Widgets"); cell (Number 42.5) ] ]

workbook [ data ] |> Workbook.save "out.xlsx"
```

`cell`/`row` are members on `SheetDsl` (brought into scope with `open type`, since plain
F# `let` functions can't have optional parameters) with optional `?col`/`?style`/`?index`.
`sheet` folds a `SheetItem list` (rows, `Table`, `EmbeddedChart`, `EmbeddedImage`,
`EmbeddedPivotTable`, `SparklineGroup`, `Protect`, `PageSetup`, `Freeze`, `ColumnWidth`,
`autoFilter`, `conditionalFormat`, `dataValidation`, `hyperlink`, `comment`) into a
`Worksheet`. `withDefinedNames`/`withProtection`/`withVbaProject` are pipe-friendly
`Workbook -> Workbook` helpers for the workbook-level (not per-sheet) features.

### XML surface (`Xml.fs`/`Xml.xsd`)

A third way to build/read a `Workbook`, alongside writing F#/C# directly and code
generation - plain XML against a real embedded schema. Two motivating uses: (1) build an
`.xlsx` from XML a transform engine (e.g. XSLT) already produces, no code required; (2)
convert an existing `.xlsx` to XML for text-based diffing/version control (`.xlsx` is a
binary ZIP, so `git diff` on one is useless) - `Xml.ofWorkbook`'s output is
deterministically ordered (sorted by cell position, or by name for defined names)
regardless of the input `Workbook`'s own list order, so a real content change produces a
small, isolated diff rather than a spurious one from reshuffled rows/rules.

- `Xml.toWorkbook (root: XElement) : Workbook` — `root` is a `<workbook>` element.
- `Xml.ofWorkbook (wb: Workbook) : XElement` — the inverse; each is the other's exact
  round trip for everything this covers.
- `Xml.schemaSet () : XmlSchemaSet` — loads `Xml.xsd` (embedded in the assembly, not read
  from a repo-relative path) for validating either direction via `XDocument.Validate`.

Covers the same worksheet/workbook-level feature set as the rest of the F# core and the
C# wrapper (cells/styles/merges/freeze/autofilter/column-row sizing, VBA and images as
base64, defined names, hyperlinks, comments, sheet/workbook protection, print settings,
Excel Tables, sparklines, charts, pivot tables - description only, doesn't re-run the
aggregation - conditional formatting, data validation). Convention: a DU case becomes an
element named after the case (camelCased) when it carries data, or an attribute value
(also camelCased) when it's one of several parameterless alternatives, e.g.
`<cell ref="B2"><number>42.5</number></cell>`. Every scenario under
`tests/Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl.Tests/Examples/` has a committed `workbook.xml` example,
validated against `Xml.xsd` at generation time.

## C# wrapper: `Kookerella.CsOpenXmlDsl`

Namespace: `Kookerella.CsOpenXmlDsl`. Target frameworks: `net8.0`, `net10.0`. Depends on
`Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl` as a normal package reference (transitive - no extra install
step). Every type is an immutable `record`; every fluent method returns a **new** instance
rather than mutating (`cellStyle.AsBold()` returns a copy with `Bold = true`, it does not
mutate `cellStyle`). All I/O is isolated in `WorkbookIO` - `Cell`/`Row`/`Sheet`/`Workbook`/
`CellStyle` have no I/O methods of their own.

### v1 scope — full parity with the F# core

Covers: cell values (`Cell.Text`/`.Number`/`.Boolean`/`.Date`/`.Formula`), basic styling
(font, fill, border, alignment, number format via `CellStyle`), per-cell lock/hide
protection (`CellStyle.Protection`/`CellProtection` - `Locked` defaults to `true` matching
Excel's own implicit default, `Hidden` (formula hidden from the formula bar once protected)
defaults to `false`; only takes effect once the containing sheet is itself protected via
`SheetProtection`), merged ranges/freeze panes/
autofilter (`Sheet.WithMergedRanges`/`.WithFreezePane`/`.WithAutoFilter`, addressed via
`CellPosition` - zero-based, or `CellPosition.FromA1("B3")`), Excel Tables
(`Sheet.WithTables(TableEntry.Of(...))`/`TableColumn`/`TableStyle` - `Save` throws
`ArgumentException` if column count/uniqueness is violated, same as the F# core), charts
(`Sheet.AddChart(ChartEntry.Of(...))`/`ChartType`/`ChartSeries`, anchored over a range of
cells same as tables), images (`Sheet.AddImage(ImageEntry.Of(...))`/`ImageFormat` -
`Png`/`Jpeg`/`Gif`/`Bmp`, raw bytes embedded and handed back unchanged, anchored the same
way as charts/tables), pivot tables (`Sheet.AddPivotTable(PivotTableEntry.Of(...))`/
`PivotAggregation` - single row/optional column/single value field only, same scope as the
F# core; unlike everything else here `Save` actually performs the grouping/aggregation
rather than just describing a reference), sparklines
(`Sheet.AddSparklineGroup(new SparklineGroupEntry(SparklineCell.Of(...)))`/`SparklineStyle`/
`SparklineType` - `Line`/`Column`/`WinLoss`, grouped so several can be styled together at
once), conditional formatting (`Sheet.AddConditionalFormat(ConditionalFormatEntry.Of(...))`/
`ConditionalFormatRule` - a closed set of cases (`CellValueRule`/`FormulaRule`/`ColorScale2`/
`ColorScale3`/`DataBarRule`/`DuplicateValuesRule`/`UniqueValuesRule`), same sealed-hierarchy
pattern as `CellValue`; icon sets/top-bottom-N/text-blank-error rules aren't modeled), data
validation (`Sheet.AddDataValidation(DataValidationEntry.Of(...))`/`ValidationKind` - a
closed set of cases (`ListValidation`/`ListFromRangeValidation`/`WholeNumberValidation`/
`DecimalValidation`/`TextLengthValidation`/`CustomValidation`), plus `ValidationAlert` for
the optional blank/error/input prompt config, shared `ComparisonOperator` with conditional
formatting's `CellValueRule`; `Date`/`Time` validation and cross-sheet named-range list
sources aren't modeled), hyperlinks (`Sheet.AddHyperlink(HyperlinkEntry.Of(...))`/
`HyperlinkTarget` - `ExternalHyperlink`/`InternalHyperlink`; `Of(cellA1, target)` handles
the common single-cell case directly), comments (`Sheet.AddComment(CommentEntry.Of(cellA1,
text, author))`/`CommentEntry` - a classic OOXML `comment`/Excel "Note", not the newer
@mention/reply Comments part; `Author` defaults to `""`), print settings
(`Sheet.WithPageSetup(PageSetup.Default.With...)` - orientation/`PaperSize`/`PrintScaling`
(`ScalePercent`/`FitToPage`)/`PageMargins`/print area/header-footer incl. even-page and
first-page variants; `Sheet.PageSetup` is `null` by default, Excel's own print defaults
apply until set), defined names (`Workbook.WithDefinedNames(DefinedNameEntry.Of(...))` -
workbook-level, not sheet-level; `Of(name, formula)` is workbook-scoped,
`Of(name, formula, sheetName)` restricts to one sheet), sheet/workbook protection
(`Sheet.WithProtection(SheetProtection)`/`Workbook.WithProtection(WorkbookProtection)` -
`SheetProtection`'s 15 optional flags all carry an explicit `Blocked` suffix
(`FormatCellsBlocked`, `SortBlocked`, ...), a deliberate departure from this wrapper's usual
"mirror F# field names" convention to avoid the F# core's inverted-meaning footgun
(`FormatCells = true` means formatting becomes *blocked*, not enabled); `WorkbookProtection`'s
`LockStructure`/`LockWindows` needed no renaming. Both `Password` fields are hashed with a
legacy, non-reversible algorithm on save and always read back `null` after load), VBA as
opaque bytes (`Workbook.WithVbaProject(byte[])`, save to an `.xlsm` path), `WorkbookIO.Save`/
`Load`, and code generation (`CsCodeGen.Generate(referenceLines, outputFileName, workbook)` -
the C# equivalent of `Workbook.generateScript`, covering everything this wrapper models;
emits a .NET 10 "file-based app" runnable via `dotnet run script.cs`, not an F# script).

### Building a workbook

```csharp
using Kookerella.CsOpenXmlDsl;

var headerStyle = CellStyle.Default.AsBold().WithFillColor(new RgbColor(220, 220, 220));

var sheet = Sheet.Create("Sheet1",
    Row.Of(Cell.Text("Item").WithStyle(headerStyle), Cell.Text("Amount").WithStyle(headerStyle)),
    Row.Of(Cell.Text("Widgets"), Cell.Number(42.5)));

WorkbookIO.Save(Workbook.Create(sheet), "out.xlsx");
var roundTripped = WorkbookIO.Load("out.xlsx");
```

`Cell.Column`/`Row.Index` default to `null`, meaning "next after the previous one" (same
convention as the F# core's `?col`/`?index`) — set explicitly via `.AtColumn(n)`/`.AtIndex(n)`
to jump to a specific position.

## MCP server: `Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl.Mcp`

A local (stdio) MCP server, distributed as a `dotnet tool` (`fsopenxmldsl-mcp` command,
`dotnet tool install -g Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl.Mcp`). Already listed in the official MCP
Registry as `io.github.MarkNicholls/fsopenxmldsl-mcp`. Exposes six tools:

- `create_workbook(path, sheets)` — builds an `.xlsx` from a plain row/column grid of cell
  text (a leading `=` makes a formula, `true`/`false` a boolean, a bare number numeric,
  else text). No styling/tables/charts/etc. — a deliberately minimal tool, distinct from
  the other five, which all cover the full feature set.
- `read_workbook(path)` — reads a file back as JSON using the same text convention.
- `generate_fsharp_script(path, outputFileName)` — reads a workbook via the F# core and
  returns F# source via the full DSL, runnable with `dotnet fsi`.
- `generate_csharp_script(path, outputFileName)` — the C# equivalent: reads a workbook via
  `Kookerella.CsOpenXmlDsl` and returns a self-contained `.cs` file targeting .NET 10
  file-based apps (`dotnet run <file>.cs`), referencing the published
  `Kookerella.CsOpenXmlDsl` NuGet package rather than a local path — runs on any machine
  with the .NET 10 SDK.
- `generate_xml(path)` — a plain-data alternative to the two `generate_*_script` tools:
  reads a workbook via `Xml.ofWorkbook` and returns it as XML validated against the F#
  core's embedded `Xml.xsd`. No `outputFileName` - there's no script to embed a save path
  into, just data.
- `create_workbook_from_xml(xml, path)` — the inverse: builds a workbook from XML matching
  `Xml.xsd` via `Xml.toWorkbook` and saves it to `path`. Unlike `create_workbook`, not
  limited to plain cell values - anything `Xml.fs` models can be expressed.

The same binary is also a plain CLI, without an MCP client at all: `fsopenxmldsl-mcp
convert <input.xlsx> --lang <fsharp|csharp|xml> [-o <file>] [--rebuild-as <name.xlsx>]`
prints (or saves) the same source/XML the matching `generate_*` tool would return
(`--rebuild-as` only applies to fsharp/csharp), and `fsopenxmldsl-mcp build <input.xml>
<output.xlsx>` is `create_workbook_from_xml` as a CLI command. Both run once and exit
rather than starting the server — `fsopenxmldsl-mcp` with no arguments still starts the
MCP server as before.

`create_workbook`/`read_workbook` go through the F# core directly; `generate_csharp_script`
is the only tool that goes through the C# wrapper; `generate_fsharp_script`/`generate_xml`/
`create_workbook_from_xml` go through the F# core's own `Xml.fs`/`Api.fs`.

## Load-bearing gotchas — read before generating code against any of these three packages

- **No formula evaluation engine exists anywhere in this stack.** `Formula(expression,
  cachedValue)` (F#) / `Cell.Formula(expression, cachedValue)` (C#) only ever shows
  `cachedValue` until something else computes a real one. Real Excel recalculates on open,
  so leaving it unset is fine only if a human opens the result in Excel first. For any
  headless pipeline (PDF conversion, another automated reader, anything that never opens
  the file in Excel) always pass the real computed result — the caller almost certainly
  already has the number that fed into the formula.
- **Format support is `.xlsx`/`.xlsm` only.** No legacy binary `.xls`, no `.xlsb`, and no
  password-encrypted-to-open workbooks (those aren't plain ZIP/OPC packages; opening one
  throws before this library's own code runs at all).
- **Reading is lossy for anything not modeled**, by design: features outside a given
  package's scope are dropped rather than partially/incorrectly represented. See
  MAPPING.md's "Known gaps" section (F# core) before assuming a foreign file's feature
  round-trips, and the C# wrapper's own scope list above.
- **VBA/macros are opaque bytes only**, in both the F# core (`Workbook.VbaProject: byte[]
  option`) and the C# wrapper (`Workbook.WithVbaProject(byte[])`) — no API to author, edit,
  or list macro source in either, and not exposed in the MCP server at all yet.
- **`Xml.toWorkbook` doesn't perform pivot table aggregation.** Unlike every other feature
  the XML surface covers, a `<pivotTable>` element only carries the *description* through -
  the actual grouping/aggregation only happens via `Writer`/the `Sheet` builder path (i.e.
  building the equivalent `Workbook` value directly and calling `Workbook.save`), same as
  `Xml.ofWorkbook`/`Reader` never re-run it either.
- **Pivot tables (F# core only) perform real aggregation** (Sum/Count/CountNumbers/
  Average/Min/Max) but are deliberately capped at one row field, at most one column field,
  and one value field.
- **All three packages are pre-1.0** — expect breaking changes between minor versions
  until a 1.0 is tagged.

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md) — full quick-start with runnable examples for every F# core
  feature (formulas, tables, charts, images, pivot tables, sparklines, VBA, conditional
  formatting, data validation, protection, print settings, defined names, code generation,
  the XML surface) plus the C# wrapper and MCP server.
- [MAPPING.md](MAPPING.md) — the authoritative list of what the F# core maps 1:1 onto
  SpreadsheetML, what's approximated, and what isn't modeled at all. Consult this before
  claiming the F# core supports a specific OOXML feature.
- [src/Kookerella.CsOpenXmlDsl/README.md](src/Kookerella.CsOpenXmlDsl/README.md) — the C#
  wrapper's own quick-start and scope list.
- [src/Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl.Mcp/README.md](src/Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl.Mcp/README.md) —
  the MCP server's tool reference and client configuration examples.
- `tests/Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl.Tests/Examples/` — one real, openable example workbook
  per F# core feature, plus the F# script that regenerates it and the equivalent
  `workbook.xml` (validated against `Xml.xsd`) - a working reference implementation, in
  three forms, for any feature described above.
- `tests/Kookerella.CsOpenXmlDsl.Tests/Examples/` — the same idea for the C# wrapper: one
  example workbook plus a `script.cs` (a real .NET 10 file-based app, `dotnet run script.cs`
  from that folder) per wrapper feature, covering everything in its v1 scope above.
